newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals says S.Africa might go to IMF for help.
newsitem.headline: Stals says S.Africa might go to IMF for help.

text.p: Central bank governor Chris Stals said South Africa might go to the International Monetary Fund for help in covering its current account deficit but still had about six months to decide.
In a television interview broadcast on Sunday, Stals said the balance of payments was the most important short-term problem.
"It would be unrealistic to base our monetary policy on the assumption that there will be a big capital inflow into South Africa suddenly again in the next six months," he said.

"So we're focusing attention on gradually reducing the deficit on the current account... It's important to see if we get the results in the trade statistics that will become available in the next two or three months.

"It's not necessary to try and force the current account into equilibrium in a very short time -- that's why we have reserves and why we have access to short-term borrowings, and we should use that to make it easier for us to bring the current account back into equilibrium, or an acceptable deficit, over the next six to nine months," Stals said.
Asked if the bank was considering applying for IMF assistance, he said:

"Yes, that is certainly a possibility and the way the situation is developing now with the current account deficit well in excess of capital inflows, I think there's full justification for us to approach the IMF if we think it is necessary.

"With the current account deficit at its present level, and the capital inflow at its present relatively low level, we can certainly go on managing the foreign reserves for another six months or so. We have lots of time to decide if we really want to approach the IMF or not," Stals said.
